content: Hexagonal architecture. Domain innermost, application defines ports, infrastructure provides adapters. Layer order DOMAIN, APPLICATION, INFRASTRUCTURE, CONTROL. No cross-layer dependencies. Port flow outbound to inbound. Severity: every CU is CRITICAL unless the CU content downgrades it explicitly.

CU means Computational Unit. A CU content block carries REQUIREMENTS, COORDINATES, IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS and ACCEPTANCE. Each numbered step names an exact file path, carries a fenced code block when it changes a file, and ends with a Prove line naming the exact command. Do NOT touch lists what this CU must not modify. Stop when is the exit condition.

REQUIREMENTS:
Deliver CU boundary checking at design time. A CU must declare its no-touch set in a form that can actually be matched, and a CU that lists its own write target as untouchable must fail before it is ever compiled. This CU creates the shared vocabulary in a new module so the design-time and run-time checks parse the same text with the same rules. Duplicating the parser in each tool is the same class of drift this feature exists to stop.

1. Create .LLMDD/tools/cu_scope.py with the shared no-touch vocabulary. The prose clauses used by the shipped bugfix-feature-5 frames become matchable globs, so the clauses carrying the most weight are the ones enforcement can reach. Two details are load-bearing and were found by running the shipped frames through this code before it was written into this frame. The shipped frames end their no-touch list with a sentence period, so entries are right-trimmed before lookup, or that clause reports as unparsed. And path normalisation strips a leading ./ by prefix rather than by character set, because a character strip deletes the leading dot of every dotfile path in this repository. Finally, scope is prose: both readers look only at what sits outside a fenced block, because a path or a Do NOT touch line inside a fence is a fixture, an assert or a shipped-code sample and never a declaration, so a frame cannot contradict its own boundary with the example it uses to prove that boundary.

```python
"""Shared CU scope vocabulary: parse a Do NOT touch list into matchable patterns."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from fnmatch import fnmatch
from typing import Final, Sequence, TypeAlias

Pattern: TypeAlias = str

NO_TOUCH_LABEL: Final[str] = "Do NOT touch:"

PROSE_TO_GLOB: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
    "any scala source": "**/*.scala",
    "any python tool": ".LLMDD/tools/*.py",
    "any itr frame or feedback file": ".LLMDD/ITRS/**",
    "any itr frame file": ".LLMDD/ITRS/**",
    "any dtr file": ".LLMDD/DTRS/**",
}

_PATHISH: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"^[\w./*-]+$")
_EXT: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"[\w./-]+\.(?:py|scala|md|json|itr|txt|sbt|yaml|yml)")
_FENCE: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"```.*?```", re.S)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NoTouch:
    entries: Sequence[str]
    patterns: Sequence[Pattern]
    unparsed: Sequence[str]


EMPTY: Final[NoTouch] = NoTouch(entries=(), patterns=(), unparsed=())


def prose_only(body: str) -> str:
    return _FENCE.sub("", body)


def _split_entries(body: str) -> Sequence[str]:
    for raw_line in body.splitlines():
        stripped: str = raw_line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith(NO_TOUCH_LABEL):
            tail: str = stripped[len(NO_TOUCH_LABEL):]
            return [part.strip() for part in tail.split(",") if part.strip()]
    return ()


def _trim(entry: str) -> str:
    return entry.rstrip(".;:")


def parse_no_touch(body: str) -> NoTouch:
    prose: str = prose_only(body)
    entries: Sequence[str] = _split_entries(prose)
    patterns: list[Pattern] = []
    unparsed: list[str] = []
    for entry in entries:
        clean: str = _trim(entry)
        mapped: str | None = PROSE_TO_GLOB.get(clean.lower())
        if mapped is not None:
            patterns.append(mapped)
        elif _PATHISH.match(clean):
            patterns.append(clean)
        else:
            unparsed.append(entry)
    return NoTouch(entries=entries, patterns=tuple(patterns), unparsed=tuple(unparsed))


def is_touched(patterns: Sequence[Pattern], path: str) -> bool:
    normalised: str = path[2:] if path.startswith("./") else path
    return any(fnmatch(normalised, pattern) for pattern in patterns)


def write_paths(body: str) -> Sequence[str]:
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(_EXT.findall(prose_only(body))))
```

The module deliberately annotates variable-length sequences as Sequence rather than as a variadic tuple form, keeping the source free of ellipsis tokens so the F2 placeholder rule stays meaningful on this module.

1. Add the dirty-tree probe to .LLMDD/tools/run-waves.py, immediately after the _cu_no_touch helper added by cu-002. It returns the set of tracked paths reported dirty, or an empty set when git cannot answer, so a git failure never blocks a wave. The porcelain status line is three status characters followed by a space, so the path starts at index three:

```python
def _dirty_paths(project_dir: Path) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Return tracked paths currently dirty, empty when git cannot answer."""
    dirty: frozenset[str]
    match _git_run("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no", cwd=project_dir):
        case Ok(out):
            dirty = frozenset(line[3:].strip() for line in out.splitlines() if len(line) > 3)
        case Err(_):
            dirty = frozenset()
    return dirty
```

2. Add the ownership index and the clash evaluator for a wave. Place both immediately after _dirty_paths. Read the steps frame for write targets, not the requirements frame. Extend the cu_scope import so write_paths is available:

```python
def _wave_write_index(cu_files: Sequence[tuple[str, Path]]) -> dict[str, Sequence[str]]:
    """Map each CU id to the write targets its frame declares in prose."""
    index: dict[str, Sequence[str]] = {}
    cu_id: str
    directory: Path
    for cu_id, directory in cu_files:
        steps_file: Path = directory / "IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS.itr"
        opened: Ok[typing.TextIO] | Err[Exception] = _open_file(steps_file)
        if isinstance(opened, Err):
            continue
        handle: typing.TextIO = opened.value
        text: str = handle.read()
        handle.close()
        index[cu_id] = write_paths(text)
    return index


def _wave_dirty_clashes(cu_files: Sequence[tuple[str, Path]],
                        baseline_dirty: frozenset[str]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return (owner, path) pairs whose write target was dirty before the run."""
    owners: dict[str, Sequence[str]] = _wave_write_index(cu_files)
    return sorted({
        (owner, path)
        for owner, paths in owners.items()
        for path in paths
        if path in baseline_dirty
    })
```
